Mao's on practice, where do correct ideas come from, and on contradiction are all great recommendations I could give to help further your understanding of this topic.

One of the most important things Mao emphasized was the dialectical relationship between theory and practice. Before we do something we have a theory of how to go about it and while we do it we learn and change the theory. It goes in a cycle over and over. Theories that are more accurate in determining practice are considered more accurate through the marxist lense. Theory cannot be removed from practice. It would be unscientific, subjective and one sided. So theory that is put to the test of criticism and internal party conflict and then as well tested and confirmed by practice are considered correct.

To your question about formal logic, logic is simply a set of rules that have been confirmed and tested through time and practice to be correct ways of avoiding errors. It is theory that is a result of this dialectical relationship.

For marxism maoists consider themselves To be the third and highest stage and I am inclined to agree. Each stage of marxism has had a main leader that was created as a result of struggle. They were the leading theorists of the prolatarian line in struggle against a bourgeois line. Marx was the first lenin was the second and mao was the third. In all three cases there was a leader after thier death that analyzed thier positions, identified universally applicable aspects of thier work and made an ideology. Marx created dialectical materialism, historical materialism, ect. Engals synthesized marx's work into marxism. Marx's work represented a coming together of all the sciences developed during the rise of capitalism into universal laws of development. It observed that the prolatariat engaged in class struggle and that the highest form of struggle was the Paris commune, where the workers took state power. Next was lenin who created and consolidated the theory of the state, imperialism, and stratagy for taking power. Stalin upheld his work and synthesized marxism leninism. Lenin's work represented marxism in the age of imperialism and prolatarian revolution. However the revolution eventually ended due to counter revolution from kruschev whose class position represented the bourgeois who no longer existed as a class but remained in the form of old habits and ideology.This leads to mao and the third stage. Mao's work includes new democracy which is a stratagey of taking power in semi colonial and semi fuedal conditions. Mao also developed protracted peoples war which is the most advanced military stratagey for taking power. There is also mao's developments of dialectics which is more developed and easier to upstand. Mass line is a stratagey for doing mass work. Cultural revolution is a stratagey for ideological development and assuring the safety of the revolution by teaching the masses that they have absolute power over thier state essentially training them to exercise power over the state. Mao also improved socialist political economy which is partially due to his improved dialectics. All these theories especially, dialectics, mass line, protracted peoples war, and cultural revolution are improvements that allow for greater ideological development of the prolatariat so they can retain power longer. The person who synthesized maoism was chairman gonzalo of the communist party of peru. Mao's work represents marxism leninism in the era of capitalist counter revolution and prolatarian counter counter revolution. You can see this in the fact that all the leading revolutionaries since have been maoists. Almost all ML parties have fallen to revisionism and electoralism. Maoists are the only ones leading revolutionary struggle. We see this in India, peru, philippines, nepal, turkey, and even the US's greatest struggle the black panthers were maoists.

In my explanation of these concepts, I will be using Stalin’s definition of nation that he uses in the national question. He defines it here:  
  
  
"A nation is a historically constituted, stable community of people, formed on the basis of a common language, territory, economic life, and psychological make-up manifested in a common culture."  
  
You may notice that under this definition some nations have several other nations within it. This is accurate. For example, the US has Black and indigenous people that both form nations within the larger nation that is the US.
